subject: MedBridge: dedicated reservation, isolation & immediate next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@medbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:32:00 -0800
Subject: MedBridge: dedicated reservation, isolation & immediate next steps

Hi Susan / Mark —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed path forward so we’re all aligned: 

Key pain points you shared
- Production latency spikes during batch ingest windows (p95 up to ~1.8s; p99 occasionally >3s)
- Need strict tenant isolation for PHI workflows (SOC2 + VPC controls required)
- Cost predictability for clinical trials cadence (bursty but forecastable monthly committed usage)

Stated goals
- Guaranteed baseline throughput to support 300 concurrent inference streams with headroom for 2x burst
- Isolation that keeps PHI on a private pool with no co-tenancy at the GPU level
- SLA targets: 99.9% availability for dedicated pool; p95 latency target ~200–300ms for real-time endpoints (we can set model-specific SLOs)

What we recommend next (concrete asks)
1) Review the attached capacity-sizing worksheet — fill in average/peak request rates and typical sequence lengths so we can size a reserved pool. (Attachment: capacity-sizing-sheet.xlsx)
2) Confirm whether your security/compliance team needs on-prem traces or if the SOC2 evidence we attached is sufficient. (Attachment: soc2-evidence.pdf)
3) We will produce a preliminary mutual action plan and a draft SOW for a 12-month reserved pool with burst credits. Can we lock a working session next Wed (Feb 18) at 10am PT?
4) Please share procurement contact and any PO cadence constraints so we can align pricing bands and contract lead times.

Tentative commercial framing (high level)
- Committed reserved GPU pool sized per worksheet + burst buffer
- Ops: Dedicated pool with tenant-level isolation + audit logs retained per your retention policy
- Escalation: Named SRE on call for production incidents during onboarding window

I’ll loop in Ben (technical lead for Dedicated) and Sean (SLA/ops) on next steps.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: soc2-evidence.pdf (PDF, 320KB)

Subject: Re: MedBridge: dedicated reservation, isolation & immediate next steps

Rachel —

Thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with our internal readout. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Burst behavior: during end-of-day batch jobs we need at least 2x baseline concurrent GPUs for ~45 minutes. Will the burst buffer you mentioned guarantee pre-warmed capacity or is it best-effort?
- Cross-region failover: we run a DR region in us-east-1. If our primary region loses capacity, what's the expected failover window and how are caches handled (KV cache warmup concern)?
- SLA/Support: 99.9% availability and an assigned SRE for the onboarding window sounds good; we also need a runbook for incident handoffs (we'll share our template).

We started filling the capacity sheet with avg/peak rates — attaching our traffic_profile.csv (internal). We can make Wed Feb 18 @ 10am PT. Procurement contact is Mark Ito (cc'd).

Susan Park
Head of ML Platforms
MedBridge Health

Attachment: traffic_profile.csv (CSV, 28KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@medbridgehealth.com>, Mark Ito <mark.ito@medbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedBridge: dedicated reservation, isolation & immediate next steps

Susan / Mark —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the traffic profile. Answers inline: 

- Burst buffer behavior: The burst is implemented as pre-allocated spare slots within the reserved commitment (configurable as "burst credits"). For guaranteed pre-warmed capacity we propose a small warmup pool (2–4 standby GPUs) which keeps KV caches warm for <5 min failover—we'll size this based on the sequence-length distribution in your CSV.
- Cross-region failover: We can enable async KV checkpointing + warmup in us-east-1; expected cold-start window for full KV cache rebuild is workload-dependent but for your profile we estimate 3–7 minutes with the warmup pool. We will include a runbook for cache priming.
- Commercial: pricing band estimate (ballpark) attached in the preliminary SOW link — final numbers depend on the committed pool size from the worksheet.

Next steps we will take this week:
- Ben: lead sizing analysis (I’ll share the worksheet inputs you provided)
- Sean: draft SLA language around availability, incident response, and escalation times
- Rachel: schedule Feb 18 working session + put together a preliminary MIP (mutual implementation plan) and SOW v0.1

Can you confirm the expected PO lead time (standard 30 days, or longer)? If 30 days works we'll aim for a March 15 start window for the committed pool and a 4-week onboarding ramp.

Prelim SOW (draft link): https://drive.redwood.ai/s/medbridge/prelim-sow-v0.1 — I’ll upload a formal DocuSign when we have the pricing band agreed.

Thanks,
Rachel
